name: Barney Purple
lede: Barney Purple is a deep, darker magenta-purple named as a variant of [[purple-munsell|Barney]], a person-tier name the 2010 xkcd survey's crowd gave to this neighboring shade.

sections.title: A modifier on a person's name
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Our data treats it as a family word built on [[purple-munsell|Barney]], with "purple" marking the darker, more saturated member of that pair, 5.8 units apart in our measurements [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the same patch as a vivid purple, about 4.8 units off, with Munsell notation 9.2P 3.7/17.0 [1].

The closest other look-alikes in our data are [[hyacinth-violet|Warm Purple]], 3.7 units away and duller, [[dark-magenta|Dark Magenta]], a darker neighbor, and [[iris-purple|Iris Purple]], more vivid and lighter [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a CIEDE2000 difference of 4, as photographed [2]. As with its sibling [[purple-munsell|Barney]], a magenta-purple this deep and saturated has no real counterpart among historical pigments [2].
